title: Gideon and the Safehouse
premise: Wendell Winterbourne, a disgraced financial-crimes investigator turned compliance ghost, notices that Flight 447 to Frankfurt has been erased mid-air—every manifest, booking, and radar trace gone while passengers' families still wait at arrivals. Chasing the vanished plane's money trail, she uncovers an inheritance scheme run by a banking dynasty that launders not cash but existence itself, deleting inconvenient people and assets from the record. Hunted by an assassin who erases witnesses as cleanly as databases erase flights, Wendell must smuggle the truth through three jurisdictions and get it filed before Frankfurt's markets open, forcing the dynasty's heir to choose between the corrupted inheritance she was groomed for and the belonging Wendell offers her. The book ends with the markets opening on a scandal that cannot be deleted—and Wendell finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Theo Villalobos is a former bank auditor who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about paper trails from a farmhouse in northern Portugal, where he claims the Wi-Fi is bad enough to keep him honest.

chapters.title: The Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Six months after 'the incident,' she audits clean money for a firm that wants no trouble, insomnia-framed nights rendered in meticulous detail. A routine flag on a charter flight catches her eye because nothing about it should be interesting. Emotional beat: numb competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The flight lands—or doesn't; every record of it evaporates between one refresh and the next, while arrival boards still list it. She pulls backups, finds them scrubbed too. First appearance of the assassin as a wrong number that knows her name. Beat: dread replacing boredom.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She realizes someone used her own compliance tools to launder the flight out of existence—the deletion bears her old department's signature logic. Her boss urges her to drop it. Beat: the horror of recognizing your own craftsmanship in a crime.

chapters.title: The Heir
chapters.summary: Ines Voss's POV. Introduced in Zurich, rehearsing a eulogy for a father who isn't dead yet, being groomed by her uncle Aurel to inherit the family's 'continuity office.' She glimpses a file labeled 447. Beat: gilded cage, first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: Wrong Number
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The assassin, Corvus, calls again—not threatening, almost courteous, offering her a way back to invisibility. She refuses and burns her apartment's hard drives, going dark in a Lisbon safehouse arranged by an old informant, Tomas. Beat: choosing danger over safety.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She maps the jurisdictional maze: Portugal won't touch it, Germany stonewalls, a US liaison named Okafor hints Washington already knows and wants it buried quietly. Everyone offers help priced in silence. Beat: institutional betrayal, isolation deepening.

chapters.title: Continuity
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Aurel walks her through the dynasty's true business: not laundering money but laundering reality—deleting assets, debts, and people. She learns Flight 447 carried a whistleblower carrying proof against the family. Beat: complicity arriving like cold water.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In the safehouse, Tomas teaches her tradecraft; their wary partnership warms into something like trust. She reconstructs the passenger list from memory fragments and a child's lost luggage tag photographed by a stranger. Beat: belonging found in exile.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. The assassin closes in on the whistleblower's surviving contact in Hamburg, methodical and oddly gentle, revealing he keeps mementos of everyone he's erased. He lets one witness live—a message, or a mistake. Beat: the hunter's hollow ritual.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opening Bell
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She calculates the deadline: evidence must be filed with the BaFin regulator before Monday's open or the dynasty's merger finalizes and the records become legally untouchable. Okafor offers extraction—for the evidence only, not her. Beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Knew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines secretly meets the whistleblower's widow, learns her father ordered the deletion to protect her inheritance—and that Aurel has scheduled his own brother's 'continuity.' Beat: inheritance revealed as a debt of blood.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Moving overland to Frankfurt, she's flagged at the Spanish-French border; a bribed officer waves her through seconds before Corvus arrives behind her. She understands she's being herded, not hunted. Beat: paranoia sharpening into clarity.

chapters.title: The Memento Box
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. His handler orders him to erase Wendell; instead he reviews his box of tokens and hesitates, haunted by the witness he spared. He begins keeping two ledgers—one for the family, one for himself. Beat: the instrument developing a conscience.

chapters.title: Safehouse Falling
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Returning to Lisbon to retrieve her backup drive, she finds the safehouse burned and Tomas missing. Grief and guilt collide; she nearly quits, then finds Tomas's contingency note hidden where only she would look. Beat: loss transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Table
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At a family dinner, Aurel tests her loyalty with a small deletion task. She fakes compliance, copying the master archive key while he watches her with something like pride. Beat: betrayal performed flawlessly, self-loathing and hope entwined.

chapters.title: Okafor's Price
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Okafor reveals Washington will trade immunity for the archive—but plans to bury it and use it as leverage, not justice. Wendell must decide whether partial truth served by power is better than full truth no one survives to tell. Beat: moral nadir.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Ordered to intercept Wendell at the airport, Corvus instead passes her the second ledger—his own record of every person the family erased—including Flight 447's crew. 'File it all,' he says. Beat: the weapon defecting.

chapters.title: Night Before the Open
chapters.summary: Wendell and Ines's alternating POV. The two women meet in a Frankfurt data center stairwell, strangers trusting each other on evidence alone. They split the archive: Ines will authenticate it internally; Wendell will file externally. Beat: alliance forged in the eleventh hour.

chapters.title: Aurel's Morning
chapters.summary: Aurel's POV. The merger proceeds; he discovers the duplication too late and unleashes everything—lawyers, regulators he owns, and Corvus's replacement. A chilling chapter of power refusing to believe it can lose. Beat: corruption at full, complacent strength.

chapters.title: Before the Bell
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A chase through the exchange district at dawn; Corvus's replacement corners her, and Corvus takes the bullet meant for her, dying as the filing uploads. BaFin's servers accept the archive at 8:59 a.m. Beat: sacrifice buying one minute.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Markets open; the stock collapses as the deletions unravel publicly; Aurel is arrested mid-toast, and Ines testifies, surrendering the inheritance to keep her name. Wendell watches from a courthouse bench, anonymous and visible at last. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Sleep Through the Night
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, Wendell rebuilds modestly—consulting for victims' families, tending Tomas's recovery, corresponding with Ines. She sleeps eight hours and wakes unafraid. Final line lands on belonging chosen, not inherited. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
